body.t: A mandolin has eight strings in four pairs, called courses. The two strings of a pair are tuned to the same note and played together, so you treat each pair as one string.
The pair nearest your face is the lowest, pair 4. The pair nearest the floor is the highest, pair 1. When a lesson says string 3, it means the third pair.

prompt.t: How do you play a pair?

options.t: Both strings at once, as one note

why.t: The two strings sit close together, so one pick stroke catches both. Together they ring as one fuller note.

hint.t: Pick the lowest pair, pair 4, and let it ring.

body.t: Each pair has to match the tuner and match itself. If its two strings disagree, you hear a slow wobble. Tune one string, then bring its partner to the same note.

hint.t: Pair 3, the D pair. Tune both strings until the wobble stops.

prompt.t: One pair has a slow wobble. What is wrong?

prompt.t: How much of the pick should show?

body.t: Push the pick down through both strings of a pair in one small motion and stop just past them. Rest the heel of your hand lightly near the bridge.

body.t: This roll is eight even notes: thumb on 3, index on 2, thumb on 5, middle on 1, then thumb on 4, index on 2, thumb on 5, middle on 1.

body.t: The forward roll moves one way, thumb then index then middle, over and over. Eight notes make thumb, index, middle twice, then thumb, index.

prompt.t: How does a forward roll fit into eight notes?

body.t: A roll is only as good as its timing. Keep all eight notes even, like a ticking clock, and land the first note of each bar right on the beat.

prompt.t: You lose the beat in the middle of a roll. What now?

options.t: Stop and start the bar over
Slow down until it feels right
Keep the right hand moving and rejoin

summary.t: Note values from whole to sixteenth, dots and rests, and the meters 4/4, 3/4 and 6/8.

body.t: The beat is the steady pulse you tap your foot to. Beats are grouped into bars, also called measures. In most music, each bar holds four beats.
Count each bar out loud: 1, 2, 3, 4. Beat 1, the downbeat, usually feels strongest. Lean into it a little.

prompt.t: What's another word for a bar?

why.t: Bar and measure mean the same thing.

prompt.t: Which beat usually feels strongest?

why.t: Beat 1, the downbeat, starts each bar.

body.t: A note's shape tells you how long it lasts. In a four-beat bar, a whole note lasts all four beats, a half note two, and a quarter note one.

prompt.t: How many beats does a half note last?

why.t: Two half notes fill a four-beat bar.

prompt.t: How many quarter notes fill a bar of four beats?

why.t: A quarter note lasts one beat, so four fill the bar.

prompt.t: Which lasts longest?

why.t: A whole note lasts four beats, a half note two, a quarter note one.

body.t: A bar can mix values, as long as they add up. A half note plus two quarter notes fills four beats: 2 + 1 + 1.
An eighth note lasts half a beat, so two fit in each beat. Count them 1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and, saying and between the beats.

prompt.t: How many eighth notes fit in one beat?

why.t: An eighth note lasts half a beat.

body.t: A sixteenth note lasts a quarter of a beat, so four fit in each beat. Count them 1 e and a, 2 e and a.

prompt.t: How many sixteenth notes equal one quarter note?

why.t: A quarter note is one beat, and four sixteenths fit in a beat.

prompt.t: How many eighth notes fill a bar of four beats?

body.t: A dot after a note adds half its value. A half note lasts two beats, so a dotted half lasts three. A dotted quarter lasts one and a half.

prompt.t: How many beats does a dotted half note last?

why.t: Half of two is one, so the dot adds one beat: 2 + 1 = 3.

body.t: A rest is a measured silence. Each note value has a matching rest: a quarter rest lasts one beat, a half rest two. Keep counting through them.

prompt.t: How long does a dotted quarter note last?

why.t: A quarter is one beat; the dot adds half of that.

prompt.t: A four-beat bar has a half note and a quarter note. What fills the gap?

why.t: 2 + 1 = 3, so one beat is left: a quarter rest.

body.t: The two stacked numbers at the start of a piece are the time signature. The top number counts beats per bar. The bottom shows which note gets one beat: 4 means a quarter note.

prompt.t: In 4/4, how many quarter-note beats are in a bar?

why.t: The top 4 means four beats; the bottom 4 makes each one a quarter note.

body.t: In 3/4, each bar holds three quarter-note beats. Count 1, 2, 3, with the weight on 1. It's the lilt of a waltz.

prompt.t: Which time signature is a waltz usually in?

why.t: A waltz counts in threes: 1, 2, 3.

body.t: In 6/8, each bar holds six eighth notes in two groups of three. It feels like two big beats, each split in three: 1 2 3, 4 5 6.

prompt.t: How is 6/8 usually felt?

options.t: Two beats, each split in three
Three beats, each split in two

why.t: The eighths group 1 2 3, 4 5 6, so you feel two strong pulses per bar.

prompt.t: In 3/4, which single note fills a whole bar?

why.t: Three beats: a half note (2) plus its dot (1).

body.t: Cedar Smoke sways in 6/8: six quick counts per bar, felt as two big beats, one-two-three, four-five-six. At 100 counts a minute it rocks like a slow boat.
Bar four holds Dsus4: a D chord with your little finger on string 1, fret 3. It hangs in the air. Bar eight drops to plain D, and the song lands.

hint.t: D at fret 3 on string 2, open B and back, then open E on string 1, and down again.

body.t: Rain on the Skylight is lo-fi: soft seventh chords over a lazy, swung beat at 72 beats per minute. Strum down on one, then down-up on three, the up a little late.
Am7 is A minor with finger 3 lifted. Cmaj7 is C with finger 1 lifted. For Dm7, finger 2 goes on string 3, fret 2, and finger 1 lies flat across strings 2 and 1 at fret 1.

body.t: Neon Laundromat stays on one chord, A7, the whole way through. A vamp like this lives on rhythm: tight, choppy strums at 96 beats per minute and a hook that dodges the beat.
Funk players call beat one the one. Hit it hard, keep your strumming hand swinging in eighths, and ease your fingers off after each strum so it goes chk.

body.t: Static on Channel Nine is punk: four power chords, palm-muted eighths, 104 beats per minute. The verse mutters on low notes; the chorus is a gang shout, so dig in.
You know C5, with finger 1 on string 5, fret 3. Slide the whole shape up two frets and it becomes D5. G5 sits at fret 3 too, one string lower than C5.

hint.t: G at fret 3 on string 1, down to D at fret 3 on string 2, then F sharp at fret 2 and D again.

body.t: Basement Weather is garage rock at 92 beats per minute: a riff on the low strings, then power chords that punch back. Rest your palm at the bridge to keep the riff tight.

hint.t: Open string 5, C at fret 3 on the same string, then open string 4, and back.

body.t: Late Bus Home is indie pop for the ride back through a sleeping city: D, B minor, G and A at 100 beats per minute. Each line starts just after the beat, so wait a breath.
Play the full B minor barre at fret 2 if you can. If not, use the top four strings: fret 4 on strings 4 and 3, fret 3 on string 2, fret 2 on string 1.

hint.t: A at fret 2 on string 3, D at fret 3 on string 2, then open E and F sharp at fret 2 on string 1.

body.t: Glass Satellites is a slow, soaring ballad at 76 beats per minute: A minor, F, C and G. Strum big on one and let it ring, then build on three and four.
Lay finger 1 flat across all six strings at fret 1 and build an E shape in front of it. Not there yet? Use the mini F on the top four strings for now.

hint.t: C at fret 1 on string 2, open E twice, D at fret 3, C again, then A at fret 2 on string 3.

body.t: Market Day borrows from highlife, the bright guitar pop of Ghana and Nigeria: G, B minor, C and D at 104 beats per minute. The hook bounces off the beat, so keep your body moving.

hint.t: D at fret 3 on string 2, open B, D again, open E, then back to D and B.

body.t: Velvet Hour is neo-soul at 74 beats per minute: four lush seventh chords stepping down, Fmaj7, Em7, Dm7 and Cmaj7. Strum once on one, then brush soft ups on the ands.
Fmaj7 is the mini F with string 1 left open. Em7 takes one finger: finger 2 on string 5, fret 2, every other string open. Dm7 and Cmaj7 you know from Rain on the Skylight.

prompt.t: The chords walk down F, E, D. Where does the loop land?

why.t: Each chord sits one step below the last, and the walk ends on C, the home chord.

body.t: Rooftop Choir is a stadium-sized anthem at 92 beats per minute. You play the chorus in C, then one bar of A lifts everything a whole step, and the chorus returns in D.

prompt.t: A key change up a whole step moves every note up…

why.t: A whole step is two half steps, and each fret is a half step. C becomes D, and G becomes A.
